locator.section: Eq. 8.2, vertical 'rH' interconversion (Eo=0.6): M+. <-> distonic ion 6.2

evidence.curator_note: McLafferty gamma-H rearrangement forming the drawn distonic ion 6.2 (a six-membered TS transfers the gamma-H, H8, from C2 to the carbonyl O6). The page shows this as a two-headed vertical arrow labelled 'rH', Eo=0.6, between the O-ionised molecular ion and structure 6.2. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: Eq. 8.2 is a thermochemical fragmentation map (log k printed above each reaction arrow, heats of formation printed below each species), not a curved-arrow figure. All electron moves here are curator-inferred from the mechanism-type label printed under the reaction arrow; none is drawn on the page. Three fishhooks (mirroring the archetypal rH): move<1> O6 odd electron into the forming O6-H8 bond, move<2> one C2-H8 electron into that O-H bond, move<3> the other C2-H8 electron back onto C2 (the new gamma-carbon radical). The migrating H is written [1H] so RDKit keeps it as an atom-mapped node.

Charge-retention branch of the McLafferty rearrangement: the gamma-radical of the distonic ion drives cleavage of the beta C3-C4 bond to give neutral propene (0.2) plus the acetone enol radical cation CH2=C(OH)+. (m/z 58, 40%). RESONANCE (convention C): the page DRAWS the enol ion with the charge AND odd electron on oxygen and a C4=C5 double bond (H-O+. over CH2=C<); this record encodes exactly that O-centred form, so the arrows relay the odd electron from C2 all the way onto O6. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: Eq. 8.2 is a thermochemical fragmentation map (log k printed above each reaction arrow, heats of formation printed below each species), not a curved-arrow figure. All electron moves here are curator-inferred from the mechanism-type label printed under the reaction arrow; none is drawn on the page. FIVE fishhooks: move<1> C2 radical into the forming C2=C3 pi bond; move<2> one C3-C4 electron completes C2=C3; move<3> the other C3-C4 electron starts the forming C4=C5 pi bond; move<4> one C5=O6 pi electron completes C4=C5; move<5> the other C5=O6 pi electron becomes the odd electron on O6. Net: propene (C1-C2=C3) leaves neutral and the odd electron ends on O6, giving the drawn enol radical cation. The C-centred resonance partner (.CH2-C(=O+H)-CH3, radical on C4, needs only 3 arrows) is the alternative localisation.

Step 1 cross-links to IMS_8_2_bidirectional_down (VERIFIED: it moves H7 from their C5=my C2 to their O19=my O6, leaving [C.]5 the gamma radical and =[O+]19([H]7) -- exactly the drawn distonic ion; its reverse is IMS_8_2_bidirectional_up). Step 2 cross-links to IMS_8_2_alpha_0_6, which cleaves the right bond (their C7-C10 = my C3-C4) and forms propene (their C1-C5=C7 = my C1-C2=C3), BUT its enol product is written '[C]10{=}[C]13(...){=}[O+.]18' giving the central carbon C13 (my C5) FIVE bonds (=C10, -C14, =O18) -- a pentavalent, RDKit-invalid over-bonded ketene-like form, NOT the O-centred enol the page draws. Encoded form matches the figure, not the MØD product. Listed in rule_mismatches.
